chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara ibn Ayn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Similar to it, and he said in his Hadith: 'And they do not permit that they marry their own mothers, if they were believers, and the wives of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in terms of sanctity are like their own mothers.'

key_terms.أَزْوَاجَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The wives of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling regarding the marriage of the Prophet's wives compared to his mothers?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the 'hurma' (sanctity/prohibition) of the Prophet's wives by drawing an analogy to biological mothers, a concept rooted in Surah Al-Ahzab. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted not merely as a prohibition of marriage but as a status of spiritual motherhood and honor, distinguishing them from other wives in Islamic law. The chain of narration through Zurara highlights the reliability of this transmission within the Usuli tradition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara Bin Ayn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

, approximately it, and he<sup>asws</sup> said in his<sup>asws</sup> Hadeeth: ‘And they are no permitting that they marry their own mothers if they were Believers, and the wives of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, regarding the sanctity, are like their own mothers’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah ibn ‘A‘yan who has said the following: “Zurarah has narrated a Hadith similar to the previous Hadith from Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

and he (the Imam) has said, ’They do not consider it lawful to marry their mothers if they are believers. The wives of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, in the matter of the above unlawfulness are like their mothers.’”
